Application hooks shape the query and its results

Long image

A

Answer

Applications can derive context, choose a configured source role, replace SQL, and edit result batches through existing extension contracts.

  1. Context fields remain separate from authenticated integration identity.1
  2. Replacement SQL is parsed and checked before routing or cache lookup.2
  3. Result processing runs on source results and raw cache replays.3

  • Derive context derive
  • Select route policy
  • Use source role execute
  • Configured choice? valid

  • Reject request deny

  • policy → resolve · Decision
  • resolve → valid
  • valid → deny · No
  • valid → execute · Yes
ValueMeaningOwner
authenticated_user = analytics_serviceAuthenticated connection identityEngine
query_context.user_id = u17App-level person or viewer referenceApplication
query_context.department = financeBusiness mapping used by policyApplication
query_context.workload = interactiveWorkload hint interpreted by callbacksApplication
target = reportingConfigured logical sourceSelector, then engine validation
backend_login = finance_readerConfigured source-role credential profileSelector, then adapter

The engine treats application values as opaque. Returning an input dialect changes parsing; it does not select a target or translate SQL.14

The repository includes a selector that looks up the user dataset and maps department to login. Compute-class selection is an additional supported decision field.54

Context is not authentication

The application must establish trust before using viewer metadata for access decisions. A user ID in a SQL remark is only a client-provided hint. Unknown, denied, or ambiguous route decisions fail. The callback cannot supply arbitrary source credentials or expand configured choices.

How can a hook change the query?

Diagram structure
  • Original query original
  • Invoke modifier modifier
  • Return decision replacement
  • Finalize query ID effective
  • Check read-only SQL check
  • Reparse replacement parse
  • Lineage and routing route
  • Reject request reject
  • check → effective
  • effective → route · Then
  • modifier → replacement
  • original → modifier
  • parse → check
  • replacement → check · Keep
  • replacement → parse · Replace
  • replacement → reject · Failure

The existing Rust table-rename example edits a cloned syntax tree. It requires a qualified input table and an explicit alias on matching references.6

Modifier resultEngine behavior
No replacementKeep original SQL and its immutable syntax tree
Replacement stringBound and parse a new immutable query in the resolved input dialect
Error, timeout, invalid SQL or unsupported statementReject; do not execute original SQL as fallback

The engine validates the effective query before generating its ID. Lineage, selection, cache eligibility, and result processing all see that effective query.27

More transformations use the same contract

An application can construct tenant-specific filters, choose a tenant schema, use a compatible summary table, or cap returned rows. It owns semantic correctness and rejects unsupported shapes when a rule is mandatory. Context is derived once. A replacement does not re-run context extraction. Policy-relevant source filters must appear in effective SQL or the validated route/scope; comment-only tags do not isolate raw cached data.

How can a hook change the result?

Diagram structure
  • Receive raw rows raw
  • Optional classification classify
  • Result hook enabled? configured
  • Validate batch validate
  • Apply application edits edit
  • Build bounded batch batch
  • Stream client rows output
  • Forward raw frames direct
  • batch → edit
  • classify → configured
  • configured → batch · Yes
  • configured → direct · No
  • direct → output
  • edit → validate
  • raw → classify
  • validate → output · Valid

The sketch uses existing native-batch operations and assumes unique text column names. The application supplies this callback; it is not a default engine policy.89

Supported editConstraint
Replace scalar textAdapter-recognized text type; validate declared lengths and byte limits
Set SQL NULLAny column; SQL NULL stays distinct from empty text
Filter rowsRetained rows keep their order
Inspect output data contextsLineage and optional model classifications describe raw results
Process successive batchesSchema stays fixed; no inserted rows or reordered retained rows

Native values avoid conversion through floating point or generic JSON. An unchanged numeric or temporal column keeps its native representation.8

Failure and replay behavior

A failed batch is rejected without a raw fallback. Previously emitted chunks cannot be retracted. The raw cache keeps original source rows. Current result processing runs again for every caller and may produce a different visible result. Optional classifications are evidence for application behavior. Mandatory engine masking remains planned.
